metadata.title: feat(ui-rewrite): create a modal with the form for adding MCP servers
metadata.author: marekdano

description: # ✨ Feature / Enhancement PR ## 🔗 Epic / Issue Related #4175 --- ## 🚀 Summary (1-2 sentences) Now I add a modal with the basic form to add a new MCP Server #### Light mode: #### Dark mode: --- ## 🧪 Checks - [x] `npm run format` passes - [x] `npm run test` passes - [ ] CHANGELOG updated (if user-facing) --- ## 📓 Notes (optional) The next step is link the form with the API

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: Should we clear the form on every close? I like the idea of clearing on submit only, in case the user closed it by accident.

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: For accessibility, consider adding a screen-reader indicator for required fielse, like so: ```html (required) ```

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body:
NIT/Optional: Might be worth replacing with a styled `radiogroup`, for better keyboard interaction (enables arrow control of this functionality). e.g.: ```html
setTransport(e.target.value)} className="sr-only peer/sse" /> setTransport(e.target.value)} className="sr-only peer/http" />
```

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body: Is it worth memoising the onchange arrow functions with `useCallback`, or do you think we'd be wasting memory for too little gain?

comments.author: gcgoncalves
gcgoncalves
comments.body:
What about replacing this ternary with and `&&`?

```tsx
{showTriggerIcon && <Plus className="h-4 w-4" />}
```

comments.author: gcgoncalves
comments.body:
Same as https://github.com/IBM/mcp-context-forge/pull/4414/changes#r3136842961, would be better as ```tsx {advancedOpen &&
...
} ```

comments.author: marekdano
comments.body: Yes, the case makes sense. I'm removing resetForm() from here.

comments.author: marekdano
comments.body: I'll leave it as it is for now. We might use some hook or custom library to handle form(s).

reviews.author: gcgoncalves
reviews.body: Might be worth checking with @a-effort if the modal animations are as intended.
